entry.title: 🧠 The End of the KV Cache? Meet "Test-Time Training" (TTT)
entry.summary: Stop scrolling. If you care about LLM architecture, you need to see this. The era of static weights might be ending. We all know the dirty secret of Transformers: Context is expensive. Enter Test-Time Training (TTT). A new repository dropped on GitHub (test-time-training/e2e), and it’s proposing a radical shift: What if your model actually learned from your prompt in real-time, updating its own weights before it answers you? Right now, when you chat with ChatGPT or Claude, the model is frozen. It reads your 100-page PDF. It stores that info in a massive temporary memory (KV Cache). It tries to attend to that memory to answer. Once the session ends, the memory is wiped. The model's weights never changed. This is inefficient. entry.title: How to Make Any CSS Element Resizable 🔧 (Without JavaScript):
entry.summary: Wanna let users resize a box by dragging its edge? Here’s how it works: 🔍 The resize property By default, elements aren't resizable. But if you want to make them resizable (like a textarea), you can use: resize: both; The second line is crucial. Resize won’t work unless you also set overflow to something scrollable (like auto or scroll). 🧪 The 3 values of resize resize: both; resize: horizontal; resize: vertical; Now users can grab the bottom-right corner and drag to resize it. The only limitation I found is that you can only resize by grabbing the corners, not the sides. But it could be useful in many cases, where we don't need that functionality. So, I'll leave that up to you.
